title: Liquid Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry (LC-MS) with Striatal Synaptosomes
author: Chuyu Chen
materials: Three mouse striata were pooled and rapidly homogenized in four volumes of ice-cold Buffer A supplemented with a Halt protease and phosphatase inhibitor cocktail (Thermo) using a Teflon homogenizer with 12 strokes.
200 µL of phase-transfer surfactant lysis buffer (PTS), supplemented with phosphatase inhibitor cocktail 3 (Millipore-Sigma) was added to each tissue sample.
Completely dry the samples in a vacuum centrifuge

Peptides were captured on a 2-cm Acclaim PepMap trap column and separated on a 50-cm column packed with ReproSil Saphir 1.8 μm C18 beads. The mobile phase buffer consisted of 0.1% formic acid in ultrapure water (buffer A) with an eluting buffer of 0.1% formic acid in 80% (vol/vol) acetonitrile (buffer B) run with a linear 90-min gradient of 6–30% buffer B at flow rate of 300 nL/min. The UHPLC was coupled online with a Q-Exactive HF-X mass spectrometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific).

The raw files were searched directly against the mouse database with no redundant entries, using Byonic(Protein Metrics) and Sequest search engines loaded into Proteome Discoverer 2.3 software (Thermo Fisher Scientific).
All data were quantified using the label-free quantitation node of Precursor Ions Quantifier through the Proteome Discoverer v2.3 (Thermo Fisher Scientific).
The supernatant (S1’) was pooled with S1.
determine protein concentration with BCA assay
injected samples into an Ultimate 3000 nano UHPLC system (Thermo Fisher Scientific).

steps.title: Animal Treatment and Tissue Collection
steps.instruction: Administer MLi-2 (10 mg/kg) or control vehicle via oral gavage to mice. After 3 hours, dissect striata, flash freeze, and store at −80°C.

steps.title: Initial Tissue Homogenization and Fractionation
steps.instruction: Homogenize striatal tissue and perform sequential centrifugation to isolate the crude synaptosomal pellet.

substeps.instruction: Homogenize tissue in Buffer A (0.32 M sucrose, 5 mM HEPES, pH 7.4, 1 mM MgCl2, 0.5 mM CaCl2) (500ul) using a Teflon homogenizer (5 strokes).
Centrifuge at 700 g, 4°C, 10 minutes.
Save supernatant (S1) and collect pellet (P1).
Centrifuge at 1400 g, 4°C, 10 minutes.
Centrifuge at 13,800 g, 4°C, 10 minutes to obtain crude synaptosomal pellet (P2) and supernatant (S2).

steps.title: Synaptic Plasma Membrane (SPM) Isolation
steps.instruction: Isolate the SPM fraction using a discontinuous sucrose gradient.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend P2 pellet in Buffer B (0.32 M sucrose, 6 mM Tris, pH 8.0) (2.5 ml) supplemented with protease and phosphatase inhibitor cocktail using a Teflon homogenizer (5 strokes).
Prepare a discontinuous sucrose gradient (0.8 M/1 M/1.2 M sucrose solution in 6 mM Tris, pH 8.0, 3 ml each).
Carefully load P2 onto the gradient.
Centrifuge in a swinging bucket rotor at 82,500 g, 4°C, for 2 hours.
Collect the SPM fraction located at the interphase between the 1 M and 1.2 M sucrose fractions using a syringe and transfer to clean ultracentrifuge tubes.
Centrifuge at 200,000 g for 30 minutes.
Remove and discard the supernatant; flash freeze the SPM pellet and store at −80°C.

steps.title: Protein Extraction and Digestion
steps.instruction: Extract proteins from the SPM pellet and perform enzymatic digestion.

substeps.instruction: Lysis using phase-transfer surfactant lysis buffer (PTS) (12 mM sodium deoxycholate, 12 mM sodium lauroyl sarcosinate, 10 mM TCEP, and 40 mM CAA).
Incubate for 10 minutes at 95°C, pulse-sonicate several times, and incubate for an additional 5 minutes at 95°C.
Centrifuge at 16,000 × g for 10 minutes and collect the supernatant.
Normalize samples to 300 ug protein each.
Digest with 6 mg Lys-C (Wako) for 3 h at 37°C.
Add 6 ug trypsin for overnight digestion at 37°C.

steps.title: Phosphopeptide Enrichment and Cleanup
steps.instruction: Enrich phosphopeptides and prepare samples for LC-MS.

substeps.instruction: Perform phosphopeptide enrichment using PolyMAC Phosphopeptide Enrichment kit (Tymora Analytical).
Dilute samples five-fold with 50 mM triethylammonium bicarbonate.
Vortex for 2 min and centrifuge at 16,000 × g for 2 min.
Collect supernatants and acidify with trifluoroacetic acid (TFA) to a final concentration of 1% TFA.
Add ethyl acetate solution at a 1:1 ratio to the samples.
Collect the aqueous phase (bottom layer) and dry completely in a vacuum centrifuge.
Dissolve the full phosphopeptide sample in 10.5 μl of 0.05% TFA with 3% (vol/vol) acetonitrile and 10 μl of each sample.
Dry the eluted phosphopeptides in a vacuum centrifuge.

steps.title: LC-MS Analysis
steps.instruction: Operate the mass spectrometer in data-dependent mode for peptide identification.

substeps.instruction: Set full-scan MS from m/z 375 to 1,500 (resolution 60,000).
Perform MS/MS of the 15 most intense ions (resolution 30,000; normalized collision energy 28%; AGC target 2E4; max injection time 200 ms; 60sec exclusion).

steps.title: Data Processing and Quantification
steps.instruction: Process MS data using search engines and quantify phosphoproteomic data.

substeps.instruction: Combine data from two search engines.
Set MS1 precursor mass tolerance at 10 ppm and MS2 tolerance at 20 ppm.

Apply search criteria: static carbamidomethylation of cysteines (+57.0214 Da); variable phosphorylation of S, T, Y (+79.996 Da), oxidation of methionine (+15.9949 Da), and N-terminus acetylation (+42.011 Da).
Perform search with full trypsin/P digestion, allowing maximum two missed cleavages; set FDR for proteins and peptides at 0.01.
Group identifications, remove redundant entries, and report only unique peptides and master proteins.

Extract phosphopeptide intensities: precursor mass tolerance 10 ppm, min 2 isotope peaks, max ΔRT of isotope pattern multiplets 0.2 min, PSM confidence FDR 0.01, ANOVA hypothesis test, max RT shift 5 min, pairwise ratio-based calculation, and max fold change 100.
Calculate fold-change between protein groups by summing total phosphoprotein abundance values and comparing the ratios of these sums.
